rv.q: What shocks in the end is that a play — yes, a play — that can, through its 80-minute running time, seem to de-prioritize plot for the poetic, also can conclude with an emotional wallop only a great playwright could produce, and only a stone could ignore.
Writers Theatre's production feels like a full-circle moment in this decorated playwright's career.
Include the special skills of the scenic designer, Courtney O'Neill, and the direction of Braden Abraham, and the result is one innovative and creative evening of theater.
It was sad and memorable, in part funny and hopeful and so was a successful production.
It's filmy and lovely to look at but, in the end, feels flimsy, unfulfilling and open to debate.

Ruhl has made some minor changes to the story, but they have a deep impact on the story. The use of current music ( with some Beatle's tunes mixed in) truly helps make it modern and will allow younger audience members to "get into it".
The production is Eurydice at its best; it plays out on stage exactly as it reads on the page.
